taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Ludwigia octovalvis; Central Texas material is commonly treated as subsp. octovalvis, also accepted by Kew.
look_here_first: Do not stop at the yellow flower. Look directly below it: the long narrow inferior ovary sits beneath the sepals and petals. Then check the strongly ridged stem and the usually 4-petaled flower.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — UT Plant Resources Center Purola Preserve flora lists Ludwigia octovalvis as naturally occurring. Travis — UT PRC Travis County Onagraceae index includes Ludwigia octovalvis. Williamson — UT PRC provides a detailed Ludwigia octovalvis subsp. octovalvis treatment.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Subspecies records are reconciled to the accepted species concept without inventing additional counties.

best_field_traits: alternate narrow oblanceolate to oblong-lanceolate leaves
long conspicuous inferior ovary below the flower
elongate capsule opening by 8 linear valves
morphology_keys.stem: Tough, strongly ridged, often pubescent and aging reddish-brown.
morphology_keys.flower: Radial yellow flower, usually 4-merous, with 8 stamens.
morphology_keys.ovary: Inferior, elongated, 4-sided and low 8-ribbed; this is the strongest family/species learning cue in Joey's sequence.
morphology_keys.fruit: Long many-seeded capsule, typically splitting into 8 linear valves.
morphology_keys.joey_field_note: Joey explicitly uses this plant to teach an inferior ovary, showing the ovary below the visible flower parts at close range.

comparisons.key_distinctions: L. octovalvis is an erect, branched shoreline plant with strongly ridged stems, narrow alternate leaves and a conspicuously long inferior ovary/capsule; L. repens is a lower creeping/submerged aquatic form.
